title_original: Threat actors use agentic AI tooling to find and abuse exposed secrets
description: Microsoft Threat Intelligence has observed threat actors using the agentic offensive security framework ARTEX to search GitHub for OAuth application secrets, which can be used to compromise the associated OAuth application and perform authenticated actions in the application’s tenant. Agents operating on behalf of threat actors then used the compromised OAuth applications to perform a variety of subsequent actions within compromised organizations.The postThreat actors use agentic AI tooling to find and abuse exposed secretsappeared first onMicrosoft Security Blog.

title_original: A Critical SSH Password Bypass Hits musl-Based Linux
description: OpenSSH 10.6p2 shipped on November 5, 2026, and it closes a critical password authentication bypass. On affected systems, anyone who can reach the SSH port can log in without knowing a password.   If you run sshd on musl-based Linux with pluggable authentication modules (PAM) disabled, Alpine Linux being the common example, upgrade today.  At Check Point Software, our testing adds two points to the public advisory. The attack needs a second account that is active and has a real password, because a stored hash alone is not enough. title_original: Inside ARTEX: How Autonomous AI Agents Are Being Used in Real-World Cyberattacks
description: AI agents are already changing how cyberattacks are carried out. Check Point Research (CPR) analyzed ARTEX, an AI-powered penetration testing platform increasingly adopted by cybercriminals and gained rare visibility into how attackers are using autonomous agents from inside their own operator consoles. The findings show that attackers can set an initial objective and leave AI agents to independently find vulnerabilities, exploit systems and pursue that goal at scale, often with very little human involvement.
